title: typeof()
summary: Returns a value's type as a string — and unlike classic Lua's type(), it recognizes Roblox engine types: "Instance", "Vector3", "CFrame", "Color3", "EnumItem"…

details.heading: Roblox-aware results
details.body: Beyond the Luau basics ("nil", "boolean", "number", "string", "table", "function", "thread"), typeof returns engine type names like "Instance", "Vector3", "Vector2", "CFrame", "Color3", "UDim2", "Enum", "EnumItem", "TweenInfo", "Ray", "DateTime", "Random" and many more.

explanation.whatItIs: The runtime 'what am I holding?' function, with full knowledge of Roblox types.
explanation.whyItExists: Roblox values would otherwise all report as "userdata" — useless for validation.
whenToUse: Validating remote arguments: `if typeof(arg) ~= "Vector3" then return end`
Debug prints when a value's origin is unclear
Branching on value category before operating
whenNotToUse: To find an Instance's class — use `:IsA("Part")` / `.ClassName` instead; typeof only says "Instance"
As a replacement for static type annotations — prefer the analyzer
tips: In Roblox code, always prefer typeof over type()
Combine with table-driven dispatch for flexible handlers
commonMistakes: Expecting typeof(part) == "Part" — it's "Instance"; use IsA for class checks

examples.title: typeof in action
examples.code:
print(typeof(5))                       --> number
print(typeof("hi"))                    --> string
print(typeof(workspace))               --> Instance
print(typeof(Vector3.new()))           --> Vector3
print(typeof(CFrame.new()))            --> CFrame
print(typeof(Enum.PartType.Ball))      --> EnumItem
print(typeof(Color3.new(1, 0, 0)))     --> Color3

local part = Instance.new("Part")
print(typeof(part))                    --> Instance
print(part:IsA("BasePart"))            --> true   (class-level check)
